Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Audit logging capabilities & SOC 2 / GDPR follow-up — post-call recap

Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for taking the call today — good to meet the Acme security and infra leads. Quick recap and proposed next steps while it’s fresh: 

1) What we covered (short):
- Audit logging: admin activity logs, API request logs, model inference request metadata, workspace/project-level audit trails.
- Export/ingest: native S3/Cloud storage export and an event streaming option for SIEM/ELK.
- Immutability & retention: append-only write model for audit entries, retention policies per-tenant, and exportable WORM-compatible objects.
- Compliance posture: Redwood has a current SOC 2 Type II report (2026) and supports GDPR data processing controls; HIPAA support via BAAs for qualifying accounts.

2) Items you asked about (answers inline):
- Can we export raw API logs to your SIEM? Yes — exports can be scheduled or streamed.
- Are admin logs immutable? We persist audit events in an append-only store and provide export hashes for tamper-evidence; we can discuss WORM-backed storage if you require strict immutability.
- Retention controls? Configurable per-organization; default 90 days, configurable up to multiple years.
- Evidence & reports? We can share SOC 2 report under an NDA and provide policy docs + a sample of audit schema.

3) Next steps I propose:
- I’m attaching our audit-logging FAQ and the vendor security questionnaire template for Acme to fill out. (Attachment: redwood-audit-logging-FAQ.pdf; vendor-security-questionnaire-acme.xlsx)
- Schedule a 30–45m technical deep-dive with Neha (security SE) to walk through export flows, retention config, and immutability proofs.
- If helpful, we can kick off an NDA to share the SOC 2 report and more detailed architecture diagrams.

Would you be available for the deep-dive next week? I have open slots Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Thanks,

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few follow-ups from our side: 

- SOC 2: good to hear you have a 2026 Type II. Can you confirm whether the report covers the hosting environment (managed vs dedicated) and whether you have a bridge letter for 2027? We’ll likely need the report under NDA.

- Immutability: our auditors are specifically asking about WORM or equivalent guarantees for exported artifacts. When you say "append-only store and export hashes," can you share how you generate and verify the tamper-evidence (hashing algorithm, key custody, etc.)?

- SIEM integration: we operate in Splunk. Do you provide a connector or do we subscribe to the event stream and ingest via a standard Kinesis/HTTP endpoint? Latency tolerance is ~30s for audit ingestion.

- Questionnaire: thanks for the XLSX — I’ll get this to our procurement/security team to complete.

Can Neha join a call on Wednesday 08/18 at 1:00pm PT? If that slot works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include our security engineer for a short run-through.

Best,
Alice

Head of Information Security, Acme Corp

Hi Alice — great questions. Quick answers and pointers below; happy to dig into any of these on the Wed call.

- SOC 2 scope: the 2026 Type II covers our hosted Redwood API platform and the managed storage surface; Dedicated deployments have a separate evidence matrix we can share. We do provide a bridge letter for in-between audits on request. We will share the SOC 2 report under NDA — I can send our standard mutual NDA if that works.

- Immutability / tamper-evidence: audit events are written to an append-only ledger and we compute SHA-256 hashes per export batch. Hashes are signed with a Redwood-held signing key managed in our KMS; for customers with strict key custody needs we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and can provide signed manifests that reference the exported objects (object URL + signed hash). We’ll bring Neha to the call to walk through the architecture and provide a sketch of the signing flow.

- SIEM integration & latency: we support both push (HTTP/Kinesis) and scheduled bulk exports to S3. For Splunk specifically, we have a maintained ingestion guide and can provide a connector recipe; streaming ingestion typically achieves sub-5s publish times on our side and should meet your 30s tolerance.

I’ve attached the FAQ and pre-filled a few rows in the questionnaire sheet to speed review.

Proposed meeting: Wed 2027-08-18 13:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm. Neha, can you attend?

Thanks,
—Marissa
